## Natural history notes

A large bumble bee characterized by a mostly black body with yellow bands on the thorax and abdomen, smoky wings, and a fuzzy robust build. In Florida, the American Bumble Bee is found in prairies, pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, gardens, farms, and other open habitats with abundant flowering plants. It is an important native pollinator, with workers collecting nectar and pollen from many wildflowers and crops, while colonies nest in abandoned rodent burrows, grass tussocks, or other sheltered cavities near the ground.
